reason: The plants need shelter before laboratory power is reduced, and the charged heat store seems useful for keeping their nook warm.
expectation: I expect the heat store to be placed inside the growing nook and help warm the plants, though I don't know whether other preparations are needed first.

alternatives.reason: Moving the lettuce into the nook also seems like a useful way to shelter it.
The battery is relevant to the reserve, but the introduction suggests preparing the plants and core first.

effect: The heat store created a buffered growing nook, so I can continue preparing the plants for reduced power.
reaction: The result is reassuring, though it doesn't explain how much warmth the nook will retain.
reason: The lettuce needs shelter, and placing it inside the buffered nook seems like a direct way to prepare it.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to be placed in the warmed nook; the potato trough may still need to be moved separately.

alternatives.reason: The potato trough also needs shelter and seems equally reasonable to move first.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its roots wet and the heat store warming its space; the potato trough still needs shelter.
reaction: The detail about keeping the trough level makes the move feel practical.
reason: The potato trough also needs shelter before laboratory power is reduced.
expectation: I expect the potato trough to be placed inside the buffered growing nook alongside the lettuce.

alternatives.reason: The service trench may need attention, but its purpose here is less clear than sheltering the potatoes.

effect: Both troughs are sheltered, with the potato cover and support still in place. I can now attend to the remaining power preparations.
reaction: The detail about fitting the deeper trough beside the lettuce makes the shelter feel practical.
reason: The service trench is the remaining preparation before switching to reserve, although its connection to the core backup is not yet clear.
expectation: I expect the tool to modify or access the insulated service trench, perhaps enabling a power connection; I am unsure what it will produce.

alternatives.reason: The battery can put the station on reserve, but the introduction suggests preparing the core backup first.

effect: The service tool drained the water line rather than preparing the core backup. The inlet remains closed, and the pump and thaw checks have essential power.
reaction: I was surprised that the trench action drained the line; its purpose was not clear from the option.
reason: The battery is the only available gameplay action and appears to put the station on its planned reserve.
expectation: I expect the selector to connect the charged battery and switch the station to reserve power; I am unsure how the core's backup connection will be handled.

effect: The reserve now supplies essential loads, the fuel plant has shut down, and the laboratory circuit remains on for the cold case’s changeover. The chapter ended without showing that changeover.
reaction: I was puzzled that the result says the garden can move into the nook now, since both troughs had already been moved there.

mostWorthwhile.text: Moving the two troughs into the buffered nook was worthwhile: the descriptions showed how their roots, covers and supports remained protected.

leastWorthwhile.text: Draining the water line was confusing because the option did not make that outcome or its purpose clear beforehand.

surprise.text: I expected work on the service trench might help connect the core backup, so the drained water line surprised me.

arbitrary.text: The service tool and trench combination lacked a clear purpose when offered, even though its result explained the line’s condition afterward.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the frozen core’s power changeover is handled and what happens to the discovery.
